newsitem.title: USA: White House unveils plan for pollution cleanup.
newsitem.headline: White House unveils plan for pollution cleanup.

text.p: The White House unveiled on Tuesday a multimillion dollar programme to help clean polluted industrial sites and also appealed to Congress to approve an extra $2 billion in tax credits for that purpose.

Vice President Al Gore said the government will invest about $300 million and provide an additional $165 million in loan guarantees under the plan to develop so-called brownfield sites, many of which are located in U.S. cities.
"This is a two-year effort to spur cleanups and the redevelopment of some 5,000 of these brownfields," Gore told a news conference.
Under the programme, the federal government will review and help develop its own idled brownfield sites, contaminated urban areas given that name in contrast to pristine green fields in the country.
The programme also would provide additional funds to cities and localities for job-training, redevelopment, housing and other purposes.
"But we must do more," Gore said. "I now call on Congress to do its part."
In its proposed budget for the fiscal year starting Oct. 1, the administration included $2 billion in tax incentives to spur development of brownfield sites.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin told the news conference that Republican congressional leadership agreed to work to get the brownfields initiative passed in their recent budget talks with the White House.
